doc.title: Bobby Hutcherson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Billy Higgins's ruffs and Herbie Lewis on his albums
summary: Billy Higgins's ruffs made Sidewinder work; Herbie Lewis plays on Stick Up and Solo/Quartet.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: ruff. “What the heck are you doing, Billy?” Plays ruff ruff ruff. That’s of the secrets of how that Sidewinder – Lee Morgan Sidewinder – worked so good, because Billy could play those ruffs. Ruff ruff ruff. I said, “Man, what are you doing, starting a car or something? What the hell?” He would do it, and he’d just smile as he’d do it. It was so – it was because it was him. It would make that happen. It would kick it along. Ruff ruff ruff, and then it would smooth out and out. Ruff ruff ruff. But it was a way of kicking it along.
That sounds like a title that you used for one of your albums, The Kicker.
We did that album. We did – Herbie was on that Solo/Quartet album. That was a different album, the Solo/Quartet with McCoy.
